name: Canopy
desc: Lying on the forest floor looking straight up — four tiers of canopy hang between you and the sky, each swaying on its own rate so the gaps open and close in true parallax and the sky comes and goes through them, backlit leaves burning translucent where the sun is behind them and going near-black where it isn't, crown shyness holding a seam of sky between neighbouring crowns, and trunks converging outward to the frame edges because looking up is a perspective too; summer green, autumn fire, a moonlit nocturne, an X-ray herbarium plate, or a cyan blueprint.

energy.doc: how hard the sun burns through — leaf translucency, sunburst glare and the brightness of the sunflecks

scale.doc: size of the near leaves and sunflecks — at max, single leaves swing across the whole frame

density.doc: how closed the canopy is — at 0 the crowns are bare and it is nearly all sky, at 1 it shuts overhead

speed.doc: advection rate of the wind field and the drift of the pollen

wind.doc: how hard it is blowing — sway amplitude of each tier and the swing of the near leaves

hue.doc: leaf hue; the sky keys off its complement

x.doc: where the zenith sits — shifts which way the trunks converge

style.doc: aesthetic: high summer, green mass against a toned sky / autumn, the canopy burning gold and rust / a moonlit nocturne, leaves rimmed silver against deep blue / an X-ray herbarium plate — leaves as translucent negatives, no local colour at all / a cyan blueprint of the crown structure

seed.doc: canopy lottery — crown layout, leaf grain, trunk placement, near-leaf hang
